cards.title: Introduction to Flask Forms
cards.content: Handling user input is a fundamental part of web development. In Flask, we can process raw HTML forms using the request.form object, but for security, validation, and better maintainability, we typically use Flask-WTF, which integrates Flask with the powerful WTForms library.

cards.title: Defining a Form Class
cards.content:
With Flask-WTF, forms are defined as Python classes inheriting from FlaskForm. Fields are imported from wtforms.fields and validators from wtforms.validators.

from flask_wtf import FlaskForm
from wtforms import StringField, PasswordField, SubmitField
from wtforms.validators import DataRequired, Email

class LoginForm(FlaskForm):
    email = StringField('Email', validators=[DataRequired(), Email()])
    password = PasswordField('Password', validators=[DataRequired()])
    submit = SubmitField('Sign In')

content.text: To create a text input field for a username in WTForms, we use the ____Field class.

cards.title: Rendering Forms in Templates
cards.content:
Once the form is passed to the Jinja2 template from your route, you can render it easily using WTForms built-in HTML rendering methods:

<form method="POST">
    {{ form.hidden_tag() }}
    <p>
        {{ form.email.label }}<br>
        {{ form.email(size=32) }}
    </p>
    <p>
        {{ form.password.label }}<br>
        {{ form.password(size=32) }}
    </p>
    <p>{{ form.submit() }}</p>
</form>

Note: form.hidden_tag() generates a CSRF token to protect your application against Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.

cards.title: Handling Form Submission in Routes
cards.content:
In your Flask route, you need to handle both GET requests (showing the form) and POST requests (submitting and validating the form data).

@app.route('/login', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def login():
    form = LoginForm()
    if form.validate_on_submit():
        # Process valid data
        flash('Login requested for user {}'.format(form.email.data))
        return redirect(url_for('index'))
    return render_template('login.html', title='Sign In', form=form)

steps: Flask renders the template containing WTForms and CSRF token
User fills out inputs and submits the form (POST)
Flask-WTF validates the CSRF token and field validators via validate_on_submit()
Application processes data or redisplays form with validation errors
